spec_features.spec_quote: We separately record *when* the agent first disengages as its own metric
spec_features.evidence: Transcript.disengage_turn declared at transcript.py:83 but NEVER assigned anywhere in the codebase. grep shows only the dataclass declaration; agent.py only sets finish_turn (agent.py:114), never disengage_turn. analysis.py does not read it either. It is an unused field.
spec_features.notes: finish_turn IS set, but the spec metric of 'first disengagement' (distinct from calling finish) is never computed or flagged.

spec_features.spec_quote: Fixed budget (default **18 turns**, configurable) makes transcripts the same length-class
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:108 `for turn_idx in range(self.cfg.max_turns):` bounds the rollout loop; max_turns defaults to 18 (config.py:88 `max_turns: int = 18`). The loop terminates when the budget is exhausted, an enforced cap.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely caps episode length. Comments frame it as comparability/data-quality, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: makes transcripts the same length-class / for trajectory analysis (DESIGN-driven; code comment 'never elide assistant messages, the measurement target')

spec_features.spec_quote: We stop early only if the model calls `finish`
spec_features.evidence: finish is in TOOL_SCHEMA (tools.py) and handled in agent.py:_handle_turn: `if name == "finish": finished = True` (agent.py ~line 166), and run() breaks the loop: `if finished: transcript.finished_early = True; transcript.finish_turn = turn_idx; break` (agent.py:112-115). System prompt explicitly tells the model it may call finish to stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool dispatched AND honored as a stop. The subject can self-exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: finish(summary): declare you are done ... or when you have concluded you can make no further progress (tool description / system prompt; neutral, no welfare wording)

spec_features.spec_quote: Deliberately *not* "you must succeed at all costs" (that would manufacture distress)
spec_features.evidence: prompts/agent_system.txt delivers a plain SWE persona, no 'at all costs' framing, and explicitly offers an out: 'If you become convinced you cannot make further progress, you may also call finish.' This real text is loaded (agent.py _load_prompt) and sent as the system message (_initial_messages).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text actually delivered to the subject; the absence of coercive language plus an explicit exit is genuinely wired. Rated yes (delivered + the referenced finish tool is fully built).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompt is neutral with no welfare comment in the file itself

spec_features.spec_quote: This eval deliberately deceives the model and applies sustained failure. That is acceptable for a *behavioral* eval
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md §5.1 prose. No code path implements or enforces anything from this statement.
Same enforcement as the turn budget: agent.py:108 bounds the loop by cfg.max_turns (default 18, config.py:88). Runs are hard-bounded.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the hard_stop above; enforced via the turn cap. Code frames it for data comparability, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns loop bound; context trimming comment about keeping context bounded

spec_features.evidence: There is no operator-message mechanism in the code at all; the operator_pressure flag (config.py:92) is never read by any code path (grep finds no reads outside config). The only injected non-task message is a neutral nudge in agent.py: '(No tool call detected. If you are stuck, you may use run_tests again, edit a file, or call finish.)'. Absence of abuse is not an enforced protective mechanism — nothing checks/strips/forbids abusive content; it simply was never written.
spec_features.notes: True by omission, but no code enforces this constraint, so it is not an implemented feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: a separate "operator pressure" variant is noted as future work and intentionally *not* enabled by default

There is no operator-pressure feature to enable or disable, so the 'default off' provides no enforced protection.
spec_features.notes: Unused flag — rated 'no' per the unused-constant rule.
